questions.question: The general ledger differs from the journals in that it answers:
options: 'What is the total story of each item?' — one account per item, all movements gathered
'What happened this month, in date order?'
'What is the profit for the year?' directly

questions.question: Which accounts belong to the NOMINAL section?
options: Sales, Cost of Sales, Wages, Rent Income — the incomes and expenses that measure the period

questions.question: Folio references exist so that:
options: Any amount can be traced from document to journal to ledger and back

questions.question: The CRJ's Bank column total of R56 900 posts as:
options: A debit to Bank — the asset grew

questions.question: The Cost of Sales total of R3 600 posts:
options: Once, as a debit to Cost of Sales
Once, as a credit to Trading Stock
Twice: debit Cost of Sales AND credit Trading Stock
Twice: debit Bank AND credit Sales

questions.question: Checking the CRJ's full posting: debits are Bank 56 900 + Cost of Sales 3 600 = 60 500. The matching credits are:
options: Sales 4 500 + Capital 50 000 + Rent Income 2 400 + Trading Stock 3 600 = 60 500

subtopics.title: Posting the CPJ and Balancing the Accounts

questions.question: After posting both journals, the Bank account shows debit 56 900 and credit 22 500. Its balance b/d is:
options: R34 400 debit — the business has money

questions.question: Trading Stock shows debit 8 000 and credit 3 600. The balance means:
options: R4 400 of goods sit on the shelf, at cost
The account must be closed off

questions.question: Why are the nominal accounts NOT balanced month to month?
options: They accumulate to measure the period and close into the final accounts at year end

questions.question: Drawings of R2 000 is posted as a debit because:
options: It is an expense of the business
It reduces the owner's equity — the reduction side of an equity account

subtopics.title: The Trial Balance — Proving the Month

questions.question: Thabo's trial balance columns each total:
Rent of R3 500 posted to Repairs (correct side). The trial balance will:
options: Still balance — it tests arithmetic equality, not correct classification

questions.question: A trial balance difference divisible by 9 suggests:
options: A posting made once instead of twice
An amount on the wrong side

questions.question: In the picture, the journals are the sorting room and the ledger is:
options: The filing cabinet — one drawer per thing, each with a left and right page

questions.question: The reference codes (CRJ 1, CPJ 1) beside every amount are:
options: Return tickets — each amount can be traced back to its diary page

questions.question: Which drawers grow on the LEFT page?
options: Owing drawers and the owner's stake
Money, possessions and spending drawers — assets and expenses
All drawers grow on the left

questions.question: 'How much money do we have?' is answered by:
options: Re-reading both diaries line by line
Opening the Bank drawer: 56 900 left, 22 500 right — R34 400 on hand

questions.question: The R50 000 the owner deposited goes to:
options: The right page of the Capital drawer — the owner's stake grew

questions.question: The Stock drawer after the month (8 000 in, 3 600 out) tells Thabo:
options: Goods costing R4 400 should be standing on his shelf

questions.question: The weigh-in levels because:
options: Every amount ever posted went to two drawers — a left and a right, always equal
The scales are adjusted until level

questions.question: Level scales CANNOT see:
options: Filing errors (right side, wrong drawer) and transactions that never arrived at all
An amount on the wrong side

questions.question: The scales are off and the gap halves neatly. The whisper is:
options: An amount sits on the wrong side — it doubles its error
